title: Autotune sieve for cache keys and throttled TTL apply
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Purpose: Build an automated, safety-first pipeline that suggests cache-key normalization (key shaping), per-prefix TTL recommendations, and applies changes using a throttled, reversible rollout (sieve) to minimize cost while bounding user-facing risk. The system should produce: 1) per-prefix hit-rate forecasts and uncertainty bounds, 2) recommended TTL deltas and key-normalization rules ranked by expected cost savings and risk, and 3) an automated throttled-applier that stages changes with canary cohorts, shadow replays, and automatic rollback if quality/cost deltas violate safety gates.

Background: We have a history of manual TTL tuning and ad-hoc key adjustments leading to either missed savings or regressions. Prior artifacts explored hit-modeling and TTL autoadaptation but lacked a single safe apply mechanism that combines key normalization + TTL changes in one controlled pipeline. This ticket closes that loop for a first-class, production-ready operator.

Goals:
- Produce accurate hit-rate predictions for prefixes (90%+ within predicted band for top 100 prefixes by cost)
- Propose TTL changes that reduce token spend while keeping request latency and miss spikes within SLOs
- Implement a throttled apply that can ramp changes conservatively and rollback automatically on signal breaches
- Provide clear observability (expected vs actual hit-rate, cost delta, error/latency signals, abort reasons)

Out of scope for this ticket: model quantization, cross-region routing policies, UI polish in Console (backend and basic dashboards only).

Acceptance criteria:
- A notebook + automated job that generates per-prefix recommendations with expected cost savings and 95% confidence intervals
- A deployable service (autotune-sieve) that performs staged apply: shadow -> 0.1% canary -> 1% cohort -> 10% -> 100% with configurable dwell times and abort criteria
- Safety gates implemented: max miss-rate increase, max tail latency delta, max cost loss (negative savings threshold), and anomaly-detection trigger for traffic shape change
- End-to-end test harness using traffic replay (synthetic + sampled production traces) and a rollback proof-of-concept runbook
- Documentation and runbook added to internal docs with links to telemetry dashboards and the PR

Design notes / approach:
1) Hit modeling: use a hybrid econometric model that combines exponential decay estimators for recency with aggregate cohort-level frequency models. For each prefix we compute: baseline hit-rate, elasticity (sensitivity to TTL changes), and uncertainty via bootstrap over daily shards. Also compute an "upweight" for prefixes with heavy batching affinity (longer contexts gain more from caching).

2) Recommendation ranking: compute expected token cost saved = (expected_missing_reduction * avg_tokens_per_call * calls) * cost_per_token. Rank by expected ROI and by risk_score = uncertainty * latency_sensitivity. Expose top-N changes and provide recommended ramp schedule (more conservative for high-risk prefixes).

3) Key normalization suggestion: identify fragmentation (many near-identical prefixes with small token volumes) via entropy clustering. Suggest merge rules (e.g., strip session ids, map ephemeral suffix patterns to canonical tokens) with simulated hit-rate impact. Each rule gets a reversible transformation function and a dry-run mode (apply in shadow only).

4) Throttled apply (the sieve): an orchestration component that applies transformations/TTLs in phases. Each phase consists of: apply config to cohort, monitor metrics for dwell window, evaluate gates, and either advance, hold, or rollback. Cohorts defined by tenant / route / traffic hashing. To reduce blast radius, the sieve supports multi-dimensional throttles (time-based, traffic-percent, per-tenant cap).

5) Telemetry & signals: ingest token-level cost, per-request latency percentiles, miss-rate, batch sizes, and error rates. Create derived metrics: expected_vs_actual_hitrate, hit-delta-confidence, rolling-anomaly-score. Alerts map to the rollback engine.

Implementation plan / work items:
- Week 1: prototype hit modeling notebook; produce baseline forecasts for top-500 prefixes by spend (ENG-535828-1)
- Week 2: implement candidate recommendation generator + ranking (ENG-535828-2)
- Week 3: build sieve orchestration prototype (shadow + 0.1% canary) with safe rollback hooks (ENG-535828-3)
- Week 4: integrate telemetry gating and run closed-runbook experiments on replay traces (ENG-535828-4)
- Week 5: run limited production pilot (one tenant cohort), finalize runbook and dashboard (ENG-535828-5)

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for model components and rule transforms
- Shadow replay tests for each recommended change to compare expected vs actual
- Staging deploy using sampled production traffic with injected anomalies
- Preflight checklist before any production throttle includes: baseline snapshot, canary cohort size, dwell time, abort thresholds, and stakeholder approvals

Rollback strategy:
- Immediate automatic rollback on any gate violation observed within phase dwell time
- If automatic rollback fails (e.g., config stuck), escalation to oncall with playbook to manually revert via config service and feature flag kill-switch
- Post-incident root cause analysis: simulate the failed change in offline environment to refine modeling assumptions

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: modelling underestimates entropy of certain prefixes -> mitigation: conservative initial TTL deltas, high uncertainty prefixes require manual review
- Risk: correlated traffic shifts cause false positives for rollback gates -> mitigation: use cross-correlation with global traffic and longer dwell windows for high-variance prefixes
- Risk: key-normalization introduces semantics changes -> mitigation: require integration tests and opt-in beta with traffic shadowing before enabling for real traffic
